premises: Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations (SCCPs) of δ-lamella and γ″ phases can be achieved in a W-based refractory HEA via a tailored aging treatment.
Coherent interfaces of these nanoprecipitates facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations.
This mechanism simultaneously increases yield strength (to ~2.0–2.15 GPa) and tensile ductility (to ~15%) relative to an as-cast or conventionally aged baseline.
The baseline alloy without this treatment has lower strength (~600 MPa to 1.4 GPa) and reduced ductility (~7–10%).
